proposal.hypothesis: Li5AlO4 is a Li-rich aluminate with Al3+, a wide band gap, and no reducible or easily oxidized transition metal. Its high Li content and oxide chemistry should make it electronically insulating and resistant to oxidation near 4 V vs Li at the LiCoO2 side, with minimal interfacial reactivity expected toward Li6PS5Cl. It is the closest in-list analogue to the Li-rich oxyanion idea, since Li3PO4 is not available.

LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with Al3+ and no reducible or easily oxidized transition metal. Al-based oxide coatings are widely used on LiCoO2 and should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Al3+ oxides are also relatively unreactive toward Li6PS5Cl, so the interfacial penalty should stay low. Li3PO4 and Li5AlO4 are not in the available list, so this is the closest valid Li-rich aluminate-type insulator.

LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with Al3+ and no reducible or easily oxidized transition metal. Al-based oxide coatings are established on LiCoO2 and should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Al3+ oxides are relatively unreactive toward Li6PS5Cl, which should keep the interfacial penalty low. Li3PO4, Li5AlO4, and Li3AlF6 are not in the available list, so this is the closest valid Li-rich aluminate-type insulator.

Li2SiO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap silicate with Si4+, which is hard to oxidize or reduce near 4 V vs Li. It has no transition metal to catalyze interfacial decomposition, and its oxide chemistry should be relatively unreactive toward Li6PS5Cl. It is the closest in-list analogue to the Li-rich oxyanion idea, since the earlier Li3PO4 and Li4SiO4 candidates are not available.

LiF is a very wide-gap (about 7 eV), electronically insulating, Li-rich fluoride with no reducible or easily oxidized cation. It is thermodynamically stable against LiCoO2 near 4 V vs Li and against Li6PS5Cl, so it should give a low interfacial penalty. It is the most established in-list alternative to the unavailable Li3PO4 and Li3AlF6 ideas.
